sampling_method: Every own-result cell in frame_locations was assigned a contiguous 1-based index in reading order -- location order above, which is page order and, within a page, linear reading order (DeiT is typeset single-column throughout, so there is no two-column split to track). Within a table, indexing is row-major and, for a row, left-to-right across that row's own-result columns only; non-own columns (citation baselines, hyperparameters) are skipped without leaving a gap. That gives a population of 1..256. Ownership in this paper is a genuine per-cell question, not a per-row one, exactly the case the brief warns about: Table 5's caption states throughput is measured by the authors 'for each model' -- convnets and competing transformers included -- while the accuracy columns beside it are citation baselines for every row except the RegNetY-4/8/16GF rows (marked with a star, explicitly 'optimized with a similar optimization procedure as ours') and the DeiT rows themselves; the same throughput-is-ours-for-every-row pattern was confirmed for Table 7 by cross-checking that its im/sec values for ResNet-50, RegNetY-8GF, EfficientNet-B7, ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/16 are exact reprints of Table 5's own-measured figures, so Table 7's im/sec column is own throughout even on rows whose accuracy columns are citations; its DeiT-B / DeiT-B-384 / DeiT-B-distilled / DeiT-B-distilled-384 rows are fully own across all eight columns. Table 2's 'Teacher acc.' column is own for every row, including the RegNetY variants, because Sec. 5.2 states the default RegNetY-16GF teacher 'reaches 82.9% top-1 accuracy on ImageNet' after being 'trained with the same data and same data-augmentation as DeiT' -- a reproduction the authors ran, not a citation -- and Table 5's star note extends that to the whole RegNetY family. Table 4's disagreement matrix is a symmetric 6x6 grid; the six diagonal 0.000 entries are excluded as tautological (a classifier's disagreement with itself is structurally zero, not a measurement), leaving 30 off-diagonal cells, each counted individually even though the matrix is symmetric and several values are printed twice at mirrored positions -- each printed grid position is its own cell. A delta counts only where no absolute is printed beside it in the same passage: Sec. 5.3's '+6.3% top-1' improvement over ImageNet1k-only ViT counts (no absolute for that ViT ablation is given in the sentence), but its 'outperforms by 1% (top-1 acc.)... (85.2% vs 84.15%)' does not count the 1%, because both absolutes are printed in the same breath; the two absolutes are handled separately (85.2% counted as a new own-result printed instance in this location, 84.15% excluded as a ViT-paper citation, repeated wherever it recurs). Training time is treated as a result on the same footing as throughput (speed presented as an outcome): '53 hours' / '20 hours' (Introduction, p2) and their restatement in Sec. 6's 'Training time' paragraph (p17, plus '37 hours' and a '20% slower' delta against RegNetY-16GF) count, as does the Introduction's 'three days' and footnote 1's 'two days'; bare bounds ('less than 3 days', printed twice, Abstract and Sec. 6) are excluded as non-point values, the same reasoning used to exclude a range. Table 8's asterisked '4.3*' / '3.4*' entries are counted (a number is printed; the footnote flags training instability, it does not withhold a value). Two identical numbers can be genuinely separate cells: 85.2% is printed as a new instance in the Abstract, in Sec. 5.2 and again in Sec. 5.3, and each is its own cell in its own location; the same holds for the training-hours figures and for DeiT-B / DeiT-B-384's Table 5 row values reappearing in Table 10 at very slightly different measured precision (e.g. 292.3 vs 291.05 for the nominally same 224-squared configuration) -- two separate measurement runs, both own, both counted. random.seed(20260810); random.sample(range(1,257),15) drew {1, 3, 23, 25, 28, 49, 57, 139, 157, 166, 182, 197, 214, 216, 244}; each label below records its draw as frame_index. Page images were rendered for pages 9, 11, 12, 14 and 15 -- the five pages that between them carry the highest-density and least text-attributable draws (Table 2, Table 4, Table 5, Table 7 and Table 8, the last needing the checkmark grid read visually since Table 8's on/off columns do not extract to text at all) -- and every row/column attribution on those pages was checked against the image. Draws landing on pages 1, 2, 3 and 9 are prose sentences, which read reliably from text alone; draws on pages 10, 13 and 17 (Table 3, the unnumbered CIFAR-10-from-scratch table, and Table 10) are small, fully-populated grids whose text dump prints an unambiguous row-label-then-values sequence with no blank cells to misplace, cross-checked internally against numbers the paper restates elsewhere (e.g. Table 10's 224-squared row against Table 5's DeiT-B row), so no image was spent on them, keeping total renders at 5 of 8 candidate table pages.
